title: How OpenAI Makes Money While Fighting Apple
the_thought: Apple owns the phone doorway. OpenAI wants the next one.
hook: A giant glass phone stands on a dark plaza like a locked castle. Apple built that castle. But why is OpenAI walking up to the gate? Because the crowd already lives inside those phones. The phone is the gate. The store on the phone is the bridge. Hundreds of millions of people walk through that gate when they unlock a screen. OpenAI walks up with a glowing chat booth. At first the two could help each other. Apple needed a strong outside brain while it built its own intelligence. OpenAI needed that pocket crowd. They shook hands in June 2024. ChatGPT would live inside Apple phones. It looked like friendship. It was a rental. Apple owns the phone doorway. OpenAI wants the next one. Keep that picture. If you remember one sentence, remember the doorway. Here is the kid map. Eight steps. First, the phone castle. Second, a ticket booth where some people pay about 20 dollars a month. Third, a spinning meter that software companies plug into. Fourth, a desk tower where whole companies buy seats. Fifth, warm hands on a stage that later crack. Sixth, a fight for the same glowing face. Seventh, a sealed complaint on a court table. Eighth, a next doorway OpenAI is trying to build. Why would a chatbot company collide with a phone empire? Because the cash registers push OpenAI toward the customer. And the customer still walks through Apple's gate. So what? The strange part is a friendship that was always a rental. To understand the fight, first follow the money.

levels.name: Phone Castle
beats: Step one. The phone castle. Apple does not merely sell a shiny slab. It owns a kingdom. The hardware is Apple's. The operating system is Apple's. The store on the phone is Apple's. When you unlock that screen, you are standing in Apple's house. Kid picture: a castle with one gate. The gate is the phone. The bridge is the store. The king still holds the key. OpenAI can enter. OpenAI does not own the castle. That is the whole problem hiding in a pretty partnership photo. Why does this matter for money? Because the company that controls the doorway can shape the customer. It can decide how big the window is. It can take a cut when people pay inside the walls. It can keep the soul of the phone looking like Apple. None of that is a cartoon villain speech. It is how a platform works. Apple already proved the point for twenty years. OpenAI is trying to become a platform too. Platforms get valuable when other people have to walk through them. So two platforms are sliding toward the same person. The person is you, holding a phone. On one side, a black turtleneck and a quiet gate. On the other, a camel sweater and a glowing booth. They can smile in June and still want the same doorway. This appears to have been a cooperation that was always a competition in slow motion. The strategy suggests Apple wanted intelligence features without handing the phone to an outside booth. The strategy suggests OpenAI wanted distribution without becoming furniture inside somebody else's house. Those wants can share a stage. They cannot share a master key. So what? The strange part is a rental that looks like love. But why would OpenAI even need Apple's gate? Because a chatbot that lives only on a website is missing the pockets. Pockets are power. Power is why the fight hurts. A website is a shop on a side street. A phone is the main square. If your product lives in the square, you meet people who never meant to visit you. That is distribution. Distribution is not a nice extra. Distribution is how a 20 dollar ticket finds a stranger. Apple already owns the square. OpenAI is renting a stall. A stall can be profitable. A stall is not a kingdom. Keep that distinction in your hands. But why rent a stall at all? Because the square is where strangers already walk. We will count the cash registers next. Then the collision will stop looking like gossip. It will look like math. And the math will keep pointing back at the same object. The doorway.

levels.name: Ticket Booth
beats: Step two. The ticket booth. This is cash register one. Imagine a bright booth with a glowing window. A person walks up. They type a question. An answer comes back. That is ChatGPT as a toy people can see. OpenAI's own help pages say ChatGPT Plus costs about 20 dollars a month on the web. Speak that number. Do not invent secret seats. The booth looks free at the front. The paid line sits behind a rope. Why do people pay? Speed. Better models. More room to play. The booth sells access, not a plastic gadget. Access is invisible. But invisible products still make loud fights when someone else controls the hallway to the customer. Because the fee lives wherever the habit lives. Kid version. Free samples get a crowd. A monthly pass gets a quieter, richer line. Most people taste for free. A smaller stream walks into a glowing subscription vault. That vault is rent. Rent repeats. A person who pays every month is more valuable than a person who claps once. Drama already hides here. The booth also lives on phones. Phones have stores. Stores have rules. Stores have owners. We will meet that owner again. First understand the booth itself. The booth is loud in culture. It is not the whole cash machine. If you only watch the booth, you miss the meters. Miss the meters and you will misunderstand the Apple fight too. People fight hardest over doors that touch their real cash. Sam Altman in a camel sweater is the public face. He is not a cash register. He is a salesman for a system that bills people and companies. But why watch a ticket? Because this fee is the first cash register in the fight. Watch a small fight already. Two people stand at the booth. One wants answers for free forever. One pulls out a ticket. The rope between them is the first money wall. Soft. Clear. Real. A crowd without tickets is applause. A crowd with tickets is rent. Applause builds the name. Rent pays some of the lights. Sometimes rent still does not cover the basement computers. We will meet that basement later. Keep one sticky image. A booth with a monthly ticket. About 20 dollars. Simple. Incomplete. A funnel helps. A wide mouth of free users. A narrow gold pipe of paying users. Most people leave through the free mouth. A smaller stream enters the vault. Recurring rent is the point of that vault. One month is a snack. Twelve months is a meal. OpenAI wants the meal. Apple's store can still take a bite of a meal sold inside the castle. That is why the booth and the castle share a plot. Next we walk into the hall where the meters spin. But why does a 20 dollar ticket matter in a fight with Apple? Because a phone store can skim a ticket sold inside the walls. The web path may leave more of each dollar with OpenAI. Habits still live on the phone. Habits are another kind of key.

levels.name: Spinning Meter
beats: Step three. The spinning meter. This is cash register two. Leave the booth. Walk into a vast power hall. OpenAI owns something like an electricity station for intelligence. Thousands of software companies plug in. Every time their apps use the brain, a giant meter spins. The developer pays OpenAI. OpenAI's own help pages say API usage is separate from a ChatGPT Plus ticket and is billed on its own. Kid picture: you do not buy the power plant. You pay for the spark when you use it. That is why the meter is the image. A subscription is a monthly pass. A meter is a bite of power. Both can be huge. They are not the same machine. So what? The strange part is a company that looks like a chat toy and bills like a utility. Why does this register matter in the Apple fight? Because a developer who plugs into the meter may never open Apple's store. The money can travel on a different road. OpenAI does not want to live inside somebody else's house forever. Today, millions of people still reach ChatGPT through devices controlled by Apple, Google, Microsoft, and others. The company that controls the doorway has power. The meter is OpenAI's attempt to be the doorway for software, not only for chat. Picture the drama. An orange-vest developer snaps a cable into a glowing socket. The meter disk blurs. Coins tick. No logos on the wall. Just power. Fair competitors live in this hall too. Other labs sell sparks. A buyer can switch cables. So OpenAI must keep the brain good and the paperwork easy. That is not a king-of-everything speech. That is a market with exits. Hold the kid map so far. Booth tickets. Spinning meters. Apple has not even opened the tiny pane yet. The castle is still in the corner of your eye. When it returns, listen for a window that will not grow. But wait. Why would a meter company still beg for a phone gate? Because consumers live in pockets. Developers live in servers. OpenAI wants both. Wanting both is how a chat shop starts looking like a platform. Platforms scare other platforms. That is the plot fuel hiding in a spinning disk. One more kid picture before the tower. The booth sells a pass to a person. The meter sells a spark to a machine. A machine can call all night. A person sleeps. That is why the meter can outgrow the booth even if the booth is more famous. Famous is not the same as fat. We will see that twist in the desk tower.

levels.name: Desk Tower
beats: Step four. The desk tower. This is cash register three, and it is the one that later takes the lead. Walk into a cream office tower. Thousands of desks. Headsets. Contracts. Instead of one person buying ChatGPT, a company buys access for a team. OpenAI's public business page lists a Business plan near 20 dollars per user per month when billed by the year, or about 25 dollars when billed by the month, for two or more users. Enterprise is custom. Sales people name the price in a room you cannot see. Do not invent a secret enterprise menu. So what? The strange part is a famous booth that is no longer the fattest register. Kid idea: a year at a desk can beat a month at a booth. A booth can cancel in a week. A company can sign longer. Drama loves a cancel button. Money loves a contract. In late 2024, reporting often said consumer subscriptions were the bigger slice. OpenAI's own later fundraising note said enterprise was more than 40 percent of revenue and on a path toward parity by the end of 2026. Then the mix moved faster than that path. CNBC reported that on August 14, 2026, finance chief Sarah Friar told investors the year started near 60 percent consumer and 40 percent enterprise. Then enterprise ran harder. The lines crossed. Friar said the majority of revenue is now enterprise, according to a person in the room. CNBC also confirmed an annualized revenue run rate near 40 billion dollars after Bloomberg first reported it on August 13, 2026. Kid translation. The booth still matters. The desks now matter more. A run rate is a pace, not a finished audited year in our pack. Hold that limit. Why are desks so precious? Because they can stack seats. Because they can add meters on the side. Because a finance team that hates waste still renews a tool the staff cannot quit. Friar, per CNBC's account, said customers had moved from burning tokens for fun to watching the cost of each unit of intelligence. That is adult language for: the restaurant started counting bites. Picture the tower. A manager wants the team smarter. A finance person wants the bill smaller. They argue. That argument is healthy for OpenAI if the product is sticky. Sticky tools renew. Also picture rival helpers knocking on the same glass. Google has Gemini. Anthropic has Claude. Apple has its own Apple Intelligence story. The desk buyer can switch. So the tower is powerful and not a forever lock. Plant this seed. The Apple fight is loud. The desk money is doing heavy lifting. If you only watch the phone castle, you will think OpenAI is losing. If you only watch the tower, you will think the castle does not matter. You need both pictures. CNBC also said advertising was approaching a 1 billion dollar run rate after tests began in February. That is spice. It is not the spine. Do not let ads steal the doorway. But why still fight Apple if desks are winning? Because the castle still owns the pockets. The tower still has a weakness. A desk buyer can switch. A finance team can cap tokens. Friar's own line about cost per unit of intelligence is a warning dressed as a boast. The bites are being counted. Counting bites is how a restaurant stays alive. It is also how a customer walks out. So the desk tower is precious and not a forever lock. But why leave the tower for a handshake? Because the castle still owns the pockets. Next comes the handshake that made the castle feel like a friend.

levels.name: Warm Hands
beats: Step five. Warm hands. June 10, 2024. Apple's big developer show. OpenAI posts a partnership note the same day. Apple's newsroom posts Apple Intelligence. The public story is warm. ChatGPT will live inside iPhone, iPad, and Mac experiences. Siri can tap ChatGPT when it helps. Writing Tools can use it. Users get asked before a question is sent. Free use without an account. Paid ChatGPT people can connect accounts for paid features. Privacy language is thick. But why all the privacy speech? Because Apple wants the phone to stay Apple-shaped. IP addresses are obscured. OpenAI will not store those requests unless you connect an account, per the public notes. Sam Altman is quoted with soft words about safety and access. Tim Cook's company puts the partnership inside a privacy speech about Apple Intelligence. On stage it looks like friendship. Off stage, lawyers will later talk about options. Friendship and options can share a calendar. Why would OpenAI want this? Distribution. Apple's phones are a crowded city of pockets. A chat booth that sits inside that city can meet people who never open a separate app. Why would Apple want this? Apple needed a strong outside brain while it built its own intelligence story. Partnering looked faster than waiting. Waiting is expensive when rivals already ship chat booths. Speed looks smart until the rented helper wants the front door. They needed each other. Say that again. They needed each other. But both companies wanted control of the same thing. The user. Kid version: two kids build a clubhouse. One kid owns the yard. One kid owns the cool toys. They shake hands. The yard kid still owns the gate. The toy kid can bring toys. The gate still decides who lines up. Replay the stage like a play. Lights up. Smiles. Cameras. ChatGPT is named as a helper inside Apple experiences. The crowd claps. Clapping feels like winning. Now freeze the frame. Ask the money question. Who owns the phone doorway after the clap? Who decides how big the window is? Who decides whether Siri shouts a product name or whispers it? Who decides if Settings becomes a fat subscription pipe? There is nothing evil about a gate by itself. Gates protect privacy speeches. Gates protect brand control. Gates also collect tolls. The film is about what happens when a rented helper wants to be treated like a co-owner. If this video only showed the handshake, it would lie. Handshakes are costumes. Money watches what happens after the photo. But a costume is not a cash register, because the pane still decides the crowd. After the photo comes a pane that stays small. After the small pane comes a letter. After the letter comes a lawsuit. Keep walking.

levels.name: Glowing Face
beats: Step six. The glowing face. This is the fight for the interface. Reporting on Bloomberg's May 14, 2026 story, as written up by MacRumors, says the integration forced friction. Siri users often had to say or type the word ChatGPT on purpose. Answers showed up in small, limited windows. The full ChatGPT app still felt bigger and freer. OpenAI wanted a front door. Apple built a tiny pane. The difference between a door and a pane is the whole movie. A door lets a crowd pour through. A pane lets a face peek. Peeking is not the same as paying. Kid version. You are outside a candy store. The store says your friend can help. But you must shout your friend's full name before the window cracks. Then the window only shows a little candy, not the whole shelf. That is not a technical footnote. That is drama. An OpenAI executive, granted anonymity in the reporting, called the deal a failure. The executive said OpenAI did everything from a product view, and Apple did not make an honest effort. We cannot see inside private meetings. We can hear what the papers printed. So what? The strange part is a window that will not grow. Apple's secrecy culture, the reporting says, meant OpenAI took a leap of faith about how deep the integration would go. Leap of faith is a soft phrase. In money language it means you signed before you saw the final door. Renegotiation talks stalled, per the same coverage. MacRumors also says people can subscribe to ChatGPT through the iPhone Settings app, and Apple takes a cut of that revenue. Apple's public store rules take a commission on many digital subscriptions. For large developers that cut is often about 30 percent in the first year and about 15 percent later. We do not have OpenAI's private Settings receipt. Speak the cut as a cut. Do not invent the slice for this deal. OpenAI, per people in that reporting, believed the Apple partnership could mean billions of dollars a year in subscriptions. Apple had framed the opportunity, the reporting says, in the same huge neighborhood as its Google search deal on Safari. Then the sentence that cracks the smile: it has not come close to happening. Hope: billions a year. Result: not close. That gap is a heart punch. Now lift the camera from the tiny pane to the whole face of the phone. The company that owns the main intelligence interface could shape search, shopping, recommendations, software, messages, work, and how a device feels. Visualize a phone screen turning into a glowing AI face. Apple on one side. OpenAI on the other. Both hands reach for the same glowing user. Extremely simple. Extremely expensive. But why grab a face on a phone? Because the interface is the next cash register. OpenAI also tried to step off the rented phone. In May 2025, reporting said OpenAI was acquiring io, a hardware startup tied to Jony Ive, in a deal valued near 6.5 billion dollars. OpenAI's own letter dated July 9, 2025 says the io team officially merged with OpenAI, while Ive's studio LoveFrom stayed independent and took design work across OpenAI. The strategy suggests a path from Apple, then user, then ChatGPT, toward OpenAI, then user. That is a different doorway. Kid picture. Today the chain is castle, then person, then booth. Tomorrow OpenAI would like person, then booth, with no castle in the middle. Hardware is one way to cut the middle. A new device is a new gate. A new gate is a new cash register. We do not have a public price for a device that has not shipped. We do not invent a launch date. We only know OpenAI spent a reported fortune to buy a hardware team, and Apple alleges that fortune was fed with stolen maps. OpenAI says that allegation is wrong. Hold both sentences. But why does a hardware shop scare a phone castle? Because a new gate is a new cash register. The next chapter is what happens when noticing becomes a complaint.

levels.name: Sealed Complaint
beats: Step seven. The sealed complaint. First they were partners. Then competitors. Then lawyers entered the room. But why did lawyers enter? Because a tiny pane can become a contract fight. May 14, 2026. Bloomberg reports the partnership has frayed. OpenAI lawyers are working with an outside firm on options. One path is a letter alleging breach of contract, without immediately filing a full lawsuit. No final decision, the reporting says. OpenAI still hopes to solve it outside court. That is careful language. Careful language still means a fight. The reporting also says exclusivity was never the deal. Apple looking at other chat helpers for later software is not what OpenAI named as the core grievance. The core grievance, in that coverage, is distribution, placement, promotion, and the conversion that never became a mountain. Then the temperature jumps. On July 10, 2026, Apple filed a federal complaint in the Northern District of California. The docket is Apple Inc. versus Liu. Apple sues OpenAI entities, io Products, and two former Apple people, Chang Liu and Tang Yew Tan. Apple alleges trade-secret misappropriation and breach of contract. Apple alleges a coordinated effort to use confidential hardware knowledge to speed OpenAI's consumer devices. Those are allegations. They are not proven facts in this film. But why does an allegation matter for money? Because hardware is a doorway plan. Reuters and other outlets summarized the complaint. The complaint itself is on the public docket. Jony Ive is not named as a defendant in the coverage of the suit. OpenAI disputes the story. On August 3, 2026, OpenAI published a post titled Apple is getting this wrong. But why a public post? Because the doorway fight had left the stage and entered a courthouse. It called the campaign careless, aggressive, and oddly personal. It said Apple's outside lawyers had emailed the wrong person and claimed a call with OpenAI's general counsel that did not happen. It said the specific lawsuit claims were not raised, then five months of silence, then a suit. On August 5, 2026, OpenAI and the other defendants moved to dismiss. The motion says Apple pleaded generic product categories, not protectable secrets. It says OpenAI is building something entirely new and different from anything at Apple. It says OpenAI has no use, need, or desire for Apple's trade secrets. It asks the court not to let a suit paper over a talent fight. Apple has sought a preliminary injunction. A hearing was set for October 1, 2026. As of the day this script was researched, a judge had not ruled that anyone stole anything. Kid courtroom without pretending we sat there. Two friends. One says you promised a big door. The other says look at the pane we built. Then a new stack of paper: you took our hardware secrets. Then a reply: you have this wrong. Both sides point at contracts and messages the audience cannot fully read. The audience gets the smoke. Strained. Failure. Not close. Alleged theft. Denied theft. The phone doorway is still on stage. Now there is a sealed envelope on the floor. Drama peaks here. Why does a trade-secret fight belong in a money video? Because hardware is a doorway plan. If OpenAI can talk to you without Apple's phone, Apple's toll booth matters less. If Apple can slow that hardware with a court order, OpenAI stays a tenant. That is not gossip. That is an incentive map. Apple has a right to protect secrets. OpenAI has a right to hire people and deny theft. A judge had not finished that argument when this film was researched. So we do not crown a winner. We show the table. Two stacks of paper. One glowing user in the middle. Money does not pause for drama. Money keeps walking into the last chapter.

levels.name: Next Gate
beats: Step eight. The next gate. Connect the pipes. Who controls the customer, the interface, the subscription, the transaction, the data relationship, the platform, and the next computing surface? That is the real battlefield. It is not one insult. It is not one app icon. Follow the money with a clean map. A consumer can pay OpenAI on the web for a booth ticket. A consumer can pay through a phone path where Apple may take a cut. A company can pay for desks. A developer can pay the spinning meter. Microsoft can collect a giant compute bill. Partners can take a slice. Apple can collect a store fee when the path runs through its walls. None of those arrows require a villain hat. They require a doorway. So what? The strange part is a war about a doorway, not a vibe. Now the cost problem, in one kitchen picture. Imagine owning a restaurant where every customer costs you money every time they take another bite. That is inference. But why does a kitchen belong in a money fight? Because more answers can mean more bills. Running the brain for an answer is not free. Training a bigger brain is not free either. The lights in the basement are chips and halls of servers. More usage can create more revenue. More usage also creates more cost. Audited calendar year 2025 figures, reported by Ed Zitron and described as verified with the Financial Times, put OpenAI's revenue near 13.07 billion dollars and the operating loss near 20.92 billion dollars. The same reporting put payments to Microsoft near 17.2 billion dollars that year. Speak those as about 13 billion in sales, about 21 billion lost from operations, about 17 billion toward Microsoft. Exact digits stay in the claim file. A company can grow sales and still burn cash. So what? The strange part is a rising run rate beside a basement that still eats bites. Apple did not light that basement fire. Apple is a different fire about a door. The 40 billion dollar run rate in August 2026 is a pace. It is not a public 10-K that proves profit. Honest limit: we do not have OpenAI's private Apple-channel ledger. We do not have the unreleased 2024 contract text. We have a partnership announcement, a strained-partnership report, a federal complaint, a motion to dismiss, a CFO quote on mix shift via journalism, a run-rate figure from journalism, and audited-year loss figures from reporting. That is enough to answer the title without pretending we sat in the boardroom. So how does OpenAI make money while fighting Apple? It sells booth tickets. It sells spinning meters. It sells desk contracts. It still uses phone distribution where it can. It argues with Apple about a door that stayed too small. It tries to build hardware so the next interface is not rented. And it grows the part of the machine Apple does not fully control. The deeper answer is this. OpenAI is not simply selling a chatbot. It is trying to become a platform through which people interact with intelligence. Platforms become enormously valuable when other businesses and consumers depend on them. Apple understands this extremely well. Because Apple already owns one of the greatest platforms ever built. That is why the relationship is so fascinating. The fight between Apple and OpenAI is not really about one lawsuit, one app, or one AI feature. It is about who owns the doorway. For twenty years, Apple has owned one of the most valuable doorways in technology. OpenAI is trying to build the next one. Apple owns the phone doorway. OpenAI wants the next one. If that next doorway works, the way OpenAI makes money could look very different from a 20 dollar booth ticket sold through somebody else's gate. Watch the key. Then watch where the cash actually walks. The booth was the costume. The desks and meters are the engine. The fight is the plot. Keep all three, or the title falls apart. So what is the honest limit one more time? We cannot see the private Apple ledger. We cannot see the unreleased contract. We cannot tell a court who wins. We can still answer the title. OpenAI makes money by selling access to intelligence in several cash registers. Its model pushes it toward owning the user. Apple already owns one of the great user doorways. That is why they could help each other. That is why they could not stay only friends. Apple owns the phone doorway. OpenAI wants the next one. That is the thought. Take it with you.

Apple can still open other helper doors. Later reporting described other chat brains being tested for the same phone castle. That is another fight for another night. This cut stays on the doorway OpenAI rented, the cash registers it actually owns, and the next gate it is trying to build. A castle that hosts many helpers is still a castle. The rent rules can change. But the key still matters, because the doorway is the prize.
